candidates: When writing `ariaLabel` values for `PopoverProvider` or any dialog-triggering component, use terminology that is consistent with how the project's product UI and documentation already describe that feature. If a component is reused in multiple contexts (e.g., a context menu that appears on stories, components, and docs), choose a generic label that remains accurate across all uses rather than one tied to a single context.

When adding a workaround for a missing or incorrect behavior in a third-party library (e.g., react-aria not injecting `aria-haspopup="dialog"` for legacy screen reader support), add an inline comment directly above the workaround explaining the reason. Reference the upstream limitation or tracking issue when possible so future maintainers can remove the workaround once the library is fixed.

When suppressing a TypeScript error caused by overly strict third-party type definitions (e.g., a library using `DOMAttributes` instead of `HTMLAttributes`, blocking valid ARIA attributes), use `@ts-expect-error` with an explanatory comment rather than a type assertion (`as SomeType`). The comment should identify why the suppression is needed and where the upstream type gap lives.

MIGRATION.md is reserved for breaking changes and deprecations only. Do not add demonstrative code examples or general feature introductions for newly added optional props; only document behavior that is removed, renamed, or will become mandatory/breaking in a future major version.

When adding MIGRATION.md entries or changelog text that cite a specific Storybook version number (e.g., 'Added in Storybook X.Y' or 'will become mandatory in Storybook Z'), verify the version number is accurate against the project's release plan before the PR is merged.
